newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikko Sec unit president says plans to resign.
newsitem.headline: Nikko Sec unit president says plans to resign.

text.p: The president of Nikko Securities Investment Trust and Management Co, an affiliate of Nikko Securities Co Ltd, said on Thursday he hoped to resign as of June 30 over its illegal bond dealings.
Hidehiro Suda told a news conference that he and three other executives involved in the incident planned to resign.
He declined to comment on his successor, saying the company's priority was to deal with the incident.
Japan's Finance Ministry said on Thursday it will ban Nikko Securities Investment Trust from establishing new trust funds for one month from June 2.

MOF said it has instructed the company to take appropriate steps to strengthen the management of its investments and to clarify responsibilities by reforming its administrative structure, in order to prevent other illegal acts.
Nikko Securities Investment Trust has said that an in-house investigation confirmed it conducted illegal dealings in 1994 involving trading in foreign bonds at prices above their market prices.
The company is five-percent owned by Nikko Securities.
